Ken Norris and Peter Driver soon asserted themselves however, and pulled away from Ibbotson and Firth. Jack Brown was well placed, closely followed by Pete Newell, making one of his rare appearances and proving that potentially he is a first class cross-country runner.
He battled to the end but had to give way to five teams, amongst whom was S.L.H. represented by Ibbotson who did the fastest time of the day and moved up from 10th to 4th.

Could it be that the activities of Ibbotson & Co. have frightened them into premature retirement? In the junior match Clive Ryan accomplished a very good double by winning both the 220 & 440 yds, the latter in 51.1s.

John has wintered well, finished 3rd in the A.A.A. indoor mile Championship behind Whetton and Ibbotson, and on 7th May wearing his first A.A.A. vest he clocked 4:10.6 to win the mile against Cambridge U.
Taylor 20th and Ibbotson 25th. The Irish team, Donore Harriers, won the team race with Messitt 6th, O'Riordan 8th and Neville 10th---Portsmouth were second, Bristol third and Derby 4th.

…hat some of the events (e.g. first visit of U.S.S.R. team, Chataway V KUTS, five men in 4 minutes or under in the Mile, Ibbotson's record Mile for example) will stay in the memory for many years to come!…
